11. STAFF ADMINISTRATIVE ITEMS
A. Adoption of Resolution Placing Proposed Ballot Measure Amending Chapter 6.68 of the Santa Monica Municipal Code on the November 3, 2026 Ballot to Maintain Existing Tax Rates; Authorize the City Council to Establish Major Event Periods When the Tax Will Apply to Corporate Bookings of More than 30 Days and to Adjust the Tax Rate During those Major Event Periods; Clarify When Returns Are Available; and Authorize the Adoption of Administrative Guidelines ADD-TO ITEM 11.A. 7/28/26
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that Council
1. Adopt a finding of Categorical Exemption pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) (common sense exemption) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines; and
2. Adopt a resolution placing a measure on the November 2026 election that would amend the City Transient Occupancy Tax to: (1) keep existing transient occupancy tax rates unchanged; (2) authorize the City Council to establish defined Major Event Periods when the tax will apply to lodging paid for or obtained by corporations and other legal entities for stays over 30 days; (3) authorize the City Council to reduce the tax rate for hotels and motels for such stays during Major Event Periods; (4) clarify that TOT refunds require a natural person to occupy the room for thirty-one consecutive days; and (5) authorize related administrative regulations; and
3. Direct the City Attorney to prepare an impartial analysis of the measure.
Staff Report Printout
a. Reso - TOT Major Event Period Ballot Measure 07.28.26
b. PowerPoint Presentation
B. Rescind Resolution Number 11785 (CCS) that was Adopted at the July 14, 2026 City Council Meeting, to Place a Proposed Ballot Measure Amending Articles XVIII and XXIII of the City Charter to Revise Requirements for Owners to Evict Tenants for Breach of a Rental Agreement Based on the Addition of New Occupants, Revise Protections for Certain Occupants Remaining in a Rental Unit After the Original Tenant Vacates, Expand Just Cause Eviction Protections to Single-Unit Dwellings, and Modify Requirements for Good Faith Owner Move-In Evictions from Non-Rent Controlled Rental Units; and Adopt a Resolution to Place a Proposed Ballot Measure Amending Only Article XXIII, Housing Policies, of the City Charter on the November 3, 2026 Ballot to Expand Just Cause Eviction Protections to Single-Unit Dwellings, and Modify Requirements for Good Faith Owner Move-In Evictions For Non-Rent Controlled Rental Units ADD-TO ITEM 11.B. 7/28/26
Recommended Actions
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1.               Adopt a finding of Categorical Exemption pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) (common sense exemption) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines; and
2.               Per Rent Control Board recommendation and City Council direction at the July 27, 2028 Special Joint Meeting of the City Council and the Rent Control Board, rescind Resolution Number 11785 (CCS) adopted at the July 14, 2026 City Council meeting and attached as Attachment C to Item 11(B) of the Agenda for the July 14, 2 026 City Council meeting, placing a measure on the November 3, 2026 ballot that would amend Articles XVIII and XXIII of the City Charter to revise requirements for owners to evict tenants for breach of a rental agreement based on the addition of new occupants, revise eviction protections for certain occupants remaining in a rental unit after the original tenant vacates, add just cause eviction protections to single-unit dwellings and condominiums, and modify requirements for good faith owner move in evictio ns from non-rent controlled rental units; and
3.               Per Rent Control Board recommendation and City Council direction at the July 27, 2028 Special Joint Meeting of the City Council and Rent Control Board, adopt a replacement resolution placing a measure on the November 3, 2026 ballot that would amend only Article XXIII of the City Charter to add just cause eviction protections to single-unit dwellings and condominiums, and modify requirements for good faith owner move in evictions from non-rent controlled renta l units; and
4.               Authorize City Councilmembers to file written arguments for or against and direct the City Attorney to prepare an impartial analysis for the replacement measure.
Staff Report Printout
a. A - July 14 2028 Staff Report
b. B-RESO 11785
c. C-Reso Article XXIII
d. Written Comments
e. PowerPoint Presentation
ADJOURNMENT

(NOT APPROVED)

  CITY OF SANTA MONICA

  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES

  JULY 28, 2026

A special meeting of the Santa Monica City Council was called to order by Mayor Torosis at 12:28 a.m., on
Tuesday, July 28, 2026, at City Council Chambers, 1685 Main Street, Santa Monica, CA.

Roll Call:  Present:  Mayor Caroline Torosis
  Mayor Pro Tem Jesse Zwick
  Councilmember Lana Negrete
  Councilmember Dan Hall
  Councilmember Ellis Raskin
  Councilmember Barry Snell
  Councilmember Natalya Zernitskaya

  Also Present:  City Manager Oliver Chi
  City Attorney Heidi von Tongeln
  Interim City Clerk Denise Anderson-Warren

 CONVENE  On order of the Mayor, the City Council convened at 12:28 a.m., with all
  members present.

 PUBLIC INPUT ON  Members of the public Zoe Muntaner and Harvey Eder commented on item
 REMAINING AGENDA  11.B.
 ITEMS:

 STAFF  11.A. Adoption of Resolution Placing Proposed Ballot Measure
 ADMINISTRATIVE  Amending Chapter 6.68 of the Santa Monica Municipal Code on the
 ITEMS:  November 3, 2026 Ballot to Maintain Existing Tax Rates; Authorize the
 BALLOT MEASURE  City Council to Establish Major Event Periods When the Tax Will
  Apply to Corporate Bookings of More than 30 Days and to Adjust the
  Tax Rate During those Major Event Periods; Clarify When Returns Are
  Available; and Authorize the Adoption of Administrative Guidelines,
  was presented.

  Motion by Mayor Torosis, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Zwick, to adopt the
  staff recommendation. The motion was approved by the following vote:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Negrete, Hall, Raskin, Snell, Zernitskaya,
  Mayor Pro Tem Zwick, Mayor Torosis
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

  1  July 28, 2026
   Motion by Mayor Torosis, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Zwick, to nominate
  Councilmember Zernitskaya and Mayor Pro Tem Zwick to write the
  Argument in Favor of the ballot measure. The motion was unanimously
  approved by voice vote, with all members present.

BALLOT MEASURE  11.B. Rescind Resolution Number 11785 (CCS) that was Adopted at
RESOLUTION  the July 14, 2026 City Council Meeting, to Place a Proposed Ballot
RECENSION  Measure Amending Articles XVIII and XXIII of the City Charter to
  Revise Requirements for Owners to Evict Tenants for Breach of a
  Rental Agreement Based on the Addition of New Occupants, Revise
  Protections for Certain Occupants Remaining in a Rental Unit After the
  Original Tenant Vacates, Expand Just Cause Eviction Protections to
  Single-Unit Dwellings, and Modify Requirements for Good Faith Owner
  Move-In Evictions from Non-Rent Controlled Rental Units; and Adopt
  a Resolution to Place a Proposed Ballot Measure Amending Only Article
  XXIII, Housing Policies, of the City Charter on the November 3, 2026
  Ballot to Expand Just Cause Eviction Protections to Single-Unit
  Dwellings, and Modify Requirements for Good Faith Owner Move-In
  Evictions For Non-Rent Controlled Rental Units, was presented.

  Mayor Pro Tem Zwick recused himself from this item due to his employment
  as Southern California Director of the Housing Action Coalition, which has
  previously advocated on the issue of rent control and tenant protections.
Mayor Pro Tem Zwick was
excused at 12:36 a.m.  Question asked and answered of staff included the changes that are now
  being proposed to Article 23 are an exact word-for-word match to what is
  already in Article 18.

  Motion by Mayor Torosis, seconded by Councilmember Hall, to adopt the
  staff recommendation. The motion was approved by the following vote:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Zernitskaya, Snell, Hall, Negrete,
  Mayor Torosis
  NOES:  Councilmember Raskin
  ABSENT: Mayor Pro Tem Zwick

  Councilmember Raskin stated his No vote was because this process has been
  in the works for a very long time. He is concerned that there are members in
  our community that need further protections and is concerned about the
  impacts over the next two years. This is an unprecedented action to remove
  a measure that has already been placed on the ballot. This was a matter that
  was vetted with a great deal of community input, a great deal of work into it,
  and he is hopeful that the city can continue to work collaboratively to find
  other avenues for protecting those vulnerable tenants over the next two years
  and hopefully get it right in 2028.

  2  July 28, 2026
   Motion by Councilmember Raskin, seconded by Mayor Torosis, to have
  Councilmembers Raskin and Snell write the Argument in Favor of the ballot
  measure. The motion was unanimously approved by voice vote, with Mayor
  Pro Tem Zwick, absent.

ADJOURNMENT  On order of the Mayor, the City Council special meeting adjourned at
  12:45a.m.

  ATTEST:  APPROVED:

  Denise Anderson-Warren  Caroline Torosis
  Interim City Clerk  Mayor

  3  July 28, 2026
